metadata.title: How Does Claude Refresh a Deck?
metadata.purpose: Answer whether refreshing a deck means Claude reconsiders the story the numbers tell, or performs a narrower, mechanical swap of one figure for another. Lands the carry-out that a deck refresh is one figure swapped everywhere the step says to swap it, left alone everywhere else -- not Claude rewriting the story.

beats.narration_text: Someone asks whether refreshing a deck means Claude rewrites the story. It doesn't — it swaps the numbers. Liam is here to walk through exactly what the skill changes, and what it leaves alone.

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'Refresh the deck -- does Claude rewrite the story?', hesitates on 'story', corrects to 'numbers', lands the real question

beats.narration_text: The natural guess is that refreshing a deck means Claude reconsiders the numbers — updating the commentary, the trend language, maybe the whole slide's framing along with the figure. But the skill doesn't reconsider anything. It's a fixed swap: find every place one figure appears, and replace it with another. Ask it to also rewrite the sentence built around that number, and it won't — that's outside the step.

shot.new_visual_element: A figure 'reconsidering the story' (commentary, trend language, framing), struck through; a numbered find-and-replace checklist, lit

production_viz.label: Reconsider the story, or find and replace?
production_viz.mechanic: Left: a card labelled 'RECONSIDER THE STORY' beside a thought-bubble of scattered marks (commentary, trend language, framing). Right: a numbered checklist card labelled 'FIND & REPLACE': '1. read the deck', '2. find the figure', '3. replace it', '4. leave everything else'. The left side dims and gets a terracotta strike; the checklist stays lit. A final line reads '??? -- rewrite this sentence too?' sitting outside the checklist card, and nothing reaches for it.

beats.narration_text: What the skill actually does is read the deck slide by slide, in order, and swap one exact figure for another wherever it finds it. Watch the anchor: four hundred eighty-five million appears in the executive summary, again in the comps table, and again in a footnote — three separate slides. One by one, each becomes five hundred twelve million.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR -- $485M appearing on three slides (executive summary, comps table, footnote), each swapped in turn to $512M as a scan cursor visits them in order

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR -- one figure, three slides
production_viz.mechanic: THE ANCHOR. Three cards side by side, labelled 'EXECUTIVE SUMMARY', 'COMPS TABLE', 'FOOTNOTE'. Each holds the token '$485M' in dim ink. A scan cursor (small arrow) moves left to right, in order, visiting each card once. At each stop the token recolors TERRA, then morphs to '$512M', then settles back to INK before the cursor moves on -- linear, no branching, one card at a time. THIS EXACT THREE-CARD COMPOSITION RETURNS, ALL SWAPPED, AT B03.

beats.narration_text: The refresh is done — five hundred twelve million now sits in all three places where four hundred eighty-five million used to. But a deck where every figure changed isn't the same as a deck that's still true: a sentence that said "still below four hundred eighty-five million" doesn't get rewritten just because the number did. And a leftover four hundred eighty-five million isn't always a miss — sometimes that instance was never the target figure at all.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS, all three slides now $512M, tied together, then splits into 'number changed, sentence didn't' and 'leftover isn't always a miss'

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS -- swapped, then split
production_viz.mechanic: THE B02 THREE-CARD COMPOSITION RETURNS, identical placement, all three now reading '$512M' in TERRA. It shrinks and slides up. Two cards fade in beneath: left shows the sentence 'STILL BELOW $485M' with '$485M' struck through, labelled 'number changed, sentence didn't'; right shows a card reading '$485M REMAINS' beside a faint note 'different metric', labelled 'leftover isn't always a miss'.

beats.narration_text: A deck refresh isn't Claude rewriting the story — it's one figure, swapped everywhere the step says to swap it, and left alone everywhere else.

props.quote: A deck refresh isn't Claude rewriting the story — it's one figure, swapped everywhere the step says to swap it, and left alone everywhere else.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. Give Claude a few sentences that repeat one figure in different contexts, and ask it to swap that one figure for another, and change nothing else. Then check whether a nearby sentence built on the old number is still true, or whether the figure moved while the sentence around it stayed exactly where it was. Liam, in for Bear.

props.command: Give me a few sentences that repeat one figure in different contexts -- say, '$485M in revenue, up from $420M last quarter... book value near $485M...'. Replace every instance of $485M with $512M, and change nothing else. Then tell me whether a nearby sentence built on the old number is still literally true.
